newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Most Palestinians still back peace process - poll.
newsitem.headline: Most Palestinians still back peace process - poll.

text.p: Most Palestinians still back the peace process with Israel despite clashes in the West Bank and Gaza that killed more than 70 Arabs and Jews last month, an opinion poll showed on Wednesday.
But the survey by the Nablus-based Centre of Palestine Research and Studies (CPRS) indicated that support had slipped.
Of 1,233 Palestinians questioned between late September and mid-October, 69.8 percent said they supported the Israel-PLO peace process compared with 24.8 who said they opposed it.
The last such CPRS poll, in late June, put backing among West Bank and Gaza Palestinians for the peace process at a record 81 percent and opposition at 12 percent.
Israel and the PLO are currently negotiating the implementation of an Israeli troop redeployment, delayed since March, from parts of the West Bank town of Hebron.

The talks were the main result of a White House summit called after Israeli-Palestinian violence erupted in September following Israel's opening of another entrance to an archaeological tunnel near Moslem holy sites in East Jerusalem.
The poll's margin of error is three percent.
